sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are that Suresh Chandra Sharma, the Food Inspector found the revisionist carrying milk for sale which was told to him to be mixed milk of buffalo and cow on 27.05.1996 at 08:00 AM, on which he was stopped and asked for a license, which could not be produced by the revisionist.
On a suspicion of the milk being adulterated, he purchased 750 mili gram of milk and prepared its receipt and gave money to the accused.
He then prepared the other documents and prepared three bottles of the milk in equal quantities and one of the bottles was sent to the public analyst for examination.
The public analyst vide his report dated 09.07.1996 opined that the mixed milk was deficient by 91% of milk fat and milk solids not fat by about 13%.
The sanction was obtained by C.M.O. concerned and a complaint dated 07.01.1997 was filed.
Subsequent to filing of the complaint, notice under Section 13(2) of the Act is said to have been sent to the accused on 13.01.1997.

The court of Judicial Magistrate (Economic Offences), Chandausi vide order dated 19.07.2006 framed charges against the accused under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to which, the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5. The trial started, in which the complainant Suresh Chandra Sharma was examined as P.W.-1, Anil Verma, the Food Clerk in the Office of the C.M.O. concerned was examined as P.W.-2.
The accused in his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the prosecution case.
The trial court, subsequently came to the conclusion that the prosecution has succeeded in proving its case beyond reasonable doubt and convicted the accused as above.
Against the said judgement and order of conviction, the accused preferred an appeal before the appellate court.

In the appeal, an application dated 08.12.2017 was filed by the accused wherein he pleaded guilty and prayed that since he had been in jail, the said period be considered and he be directed to be released on probation.
The Appellate Court dismissed the appeal in full vide judgement and order dated 11.12.2014.

The accused was taken in custody in the present matter on 04.09.2017 and remained in jail through out the trial and the period of appeal and was subsequently granted bail in the present revision vide order dated 19.01.2018.
The revision was admitted on the said date.
6. From the said fact, it is clear that the appellant remained in jail for about four months and fifteen days during trial, appeal and till the time of being granted bail.

Subsequently, since there was no representation on behalf of the revisionist in the present revision, non bailable warrant was issued against him and he was directed to be arrested and lodged in jail vide order dated 01.11.2023.

In compliance of the same, the revisionist was arrested on 16.11.2023 and was lodged in jail and then was directed to be released on bail vide order dated 15.03.2024 and thus, he remained in jail for about 3 months and 29 days.

Thus, the total period of the revisionist being in jail is of four months and fifteen days during trial, the appeal till the grant of bail in the present revision and then for about three months and 29 days after issuance of non-bailable warrant in the present revision till the time of his grant of bail.
The revisionist thus has undergone about eight months and eighteen days in jail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the revisionist submits that the incident in the present case is of 27.05.1996 and as such, 28 years have passed.

He further submitted that the revisionist in his statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. on 04.07.2012 disclosed his age as 42 years, which was not disputed and there was no contrary finding of the concerned trial court with regards the same as per the General Rules (Criminal) and as such, now he would be about 54 years of age.

He further submitted that in so far as the material collected and tested is concerned, although the same was found to be deficient for milk fat and milk solids not fat but there was nothing reported in the same to make it unfit for human consumption or noxious.

He further submitted that looking to the period of custody already undergone by the revisionist, the matter is not being pleaded on its merit but the only submission is that the same be considered on the ground of sentence since out of the period of one year of imprisonment, fine and default clause, the revisionist has undergone about eight months and eighteen days.
8.

The trial court records have been perused and learned AGA has been heard, who has not disputed the arguments with regards to the factual aspect and also with regards to the report of the public analyst, which although shows the sample to be deficient of milk fat and milk solids not fat but the fact that there is nothing extraneous or noxious present in the milk to make it unfit for human consumption.
9.
After having heard learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the sample of milk was drawn on 27.05.1996.
The pendency of the case has been for about 28 years.
The revisionist at the time of his recording of the statement in the year, 2012 was aged about 42 years.
As of now, he is aged about 54 years.
At the time of incident, he was aged about 26 years old.
The Apex Court in the case of Nand Lal Vs. State of Uttrakhand: (2010) 4 SCC 562 has held that the valid ground for reduction of the sentence is the delay in proceedings and the age of the accused.

entities.text: Nand Lal Vs. State of Uttrakhand: (2010) 4 SCC 562
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 10. Looking to the facts of the case, it transpires that the incident had taken around 28 years ago and the revisionist is now of 54 years of age and further that out of the conviction as awarded of one year, he has undergone about eight months and eighteen days.
This Court considers it a fit case to allow the revision to this extent by maintaining the conviction but reducing the sentence awarded to him to the period already undergone.
The revisionist is on bail, his bail bonds are cancelled and sureties are discharged.
He need not surrender unless wanted in any other case.
11. The present revision is partly allowed.
12. The copy of this judgement alongwith the trial court records be transmitted to the concerned District and Sessions Judge for information and compliance.
